title: GPT vs Claude Robot Task Direction Capability: First-Ever Evaluation Ranking Released
key_facts: Artificial Analysis, a US AI benchmark company, released AA-Robotics v0.1, a research preview, on 14 Oct 2026.
Models such as GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon write code to control a Hiwonder NexArm 6-axis robotic arm on 8 desktop tasks, watching through 4 cameras.
GPT-6 Astra ranked first with 69; it averaged 30 minutes and $16.36 per task; GPT-6.1 Sol cost $1.93 per task and scored 65.
Models were close to 100 times slower than humans (about 30 minutes versus 20 seconds per task) and at least about 10 times as costly.
Models often kept fiddling after a task was already complete, which sometimes caused failure.
In grasping and fine manipulation, Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 succeeded about 45 percent of the time.
quote_evidence: In AA-Robotics v0.1, GPT-6 Astra ranks first with a score of 69.
The evaluation results show that the speed of current language models to complete AA-Robotics v0.1 tasks is only about 1/100 of that of humans.
why_it_matters_hint: General AI models can now operate a robot arm, but are far too slow and costly for production.
notes: Full text read. Republished from WeChat account Robot Forward Outlook; original benchmark by Artificial Analysis was not read directly. Event 14 Oct, so score lowered.
